findings.issue: nitro ^3.0.260903-beta is pinned to the Sep-2026 beta line; npm's latest is 3.0.261029-rc, and caret ranges cannot cross prerelease tuples, so npm will not pick up the RC or the eventual stable 3.x automatically
findings.suggestion: Bump to the current RC (or pin a lockfile upgrade once Nitro 3 goes stable) and review nitro.build's 'Upgrading from Beta' breaking-changes guide; note that Vite 8/Rolldown and the RC both changed defaults (h3 v2, ocache) that could affect the production build

findings.issue: The nitro() Vite plugin is a pre-release API surface (nitro/vite, Nitro 3 beta/RC), albeit copied exactly from the official SolidStart v2 reference config
findings.suggestion: No action needed now; keep an eye on nitro/vite plugin options if any are added later, and re-verify against the SolidStart vite-config reference when upgrading nitro

findings.issue: The whole toolchain is very young: SolidStart 2 stable only since 2026-08-04, Vite 8 with Rolldown core, and transitively h3 v2 (still -rc via @solidjs/start 2.1.0's dependency) and srvx
findings.suggestion: Treat framework/toolchain upgrades as a standing maintenance item: subscribe to solid-start and nitro release notes and re-run the acceptance suite (and a production-build smoke test) on each minor bump

summary: The app's own code contains zero experimental APIs — every import is a long-stable @solidjs/router, @solidjs/start or solid-js primitive, and the server data layer sits cleanly behind lib/queries.ts and lib/server/pokeapi.ts. The only pre-release reach is toolchain-level: nitro 3.0.260903-beta, which is nonetheless the officially prescribed deployment plugin for the current stable SolidStart 2.1 (verified against npm dist-tags and the docs.solidjs.com v2 vite-config reference). Main risk is maintenance, not correctness: the caret range is stuck on the Sep beta behind the 2026-10-29 RC and will need a deliberate bump when Nitro 3 stabilizes.
